Hysteria2 and TUIC. A box that judges the flow by its first packets sees the fakes, or a ClientHello without the server name: a post-quantum ClientHello takes two Initial packets, and the second one goes first. A raycontrol node drops the fakes; for another server give them a TTL that ends before it (fewer hops than the server). Reordering does nothing under Hysteria2 obfs (no visible Initial there).

Before connecting, sends TCP SYNs or UDP datagrams to these ports of the server, in order. UDP steps may carry a hex payload: 1234/udp:68656c6c6f. SPA: 62201/spa:KEY sends one signed datagram that cannot be replayed (KEY = 64 hex digits, as on the server). Knocks again after a network change and when a connection fails. If a UDP session (WireGuard, Hysteria2, TUIC) gets no reply for the silence timeout after sending, knocks once more and logs whether the server answers again. Leave the sequence empty to disable.
